source_evidence: Conducting a thorough inquiry into an adviser’s services, fee arrangements, and investment offerings will help you select an adviser capable of serving your investment objectives.
answer: When selecting an investment adviser, compare the services and products you need with what the adviser offers, including any limitations. Ask how the adviser is paid, what fees and transaction costs you may owe, and what conflicts of interest could affect the advice. Also consider the adviser’s legal or disciplinary history. Before agreeing, read and understand the contract, relationship summary, and Form ADV Part 2 Brochure. Check both the adviser and the firm’s registration and history.
